intro: Welcome to the hangar! Pick one part from each list on the left.
Watch the numbers on the right. Every part costs money, mass and power.
shell: The shell is the crew's home, like a camper van for space.
Roomier means a happier crew, but every extra tonne has to be lifted.
lifeSupport: Life support makes air, water and warmth for the crew.
Cheap systems break more often. Think of a cheap tent in a storm.
power: The battery is like a phone battery for the whole capsule.
Add up what your parts use. The battery has to cover all of it.
comms: The radio is your phone line to Mission Control.
A better radio means clearer calls and earlier warnings, but it uses more power.
computer: The flight computer is the capsule's brain. It steers and checks every system.
Cheap computers run cheap code. Software bugs have ended real missions.
mass: A rocket can only lift so much, like a car with a roof box.
Keep your capsule lighter than the rocket can lift, with room to spare.
